ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: Four coupled physical operators: (1) Antislope Graben & Relief-Normalized Crest-Toe Scarp Dipole (upface_max*(0.25+coh100)/(cross_max+0.08), sqrt(lapneg_max*lappos_max), step_max/sqrt(relief+9)) + 8-azimuth 1.1 km flank-subtracted strike-worm filter bank on seam-free 1m/10m topography; (2) Contrarian Faulds-Hinz (2015) Structural-Intersection & Hydrothermal Conduit Operator I_vent = sqrt(max(W_(1),0)*max(W_perp,0)) capturing conjugate/orthogonal 2nd-azimuth fault intersections & horse-tail splays coupled with shallow hydrothermal magnetite oxidation (TMI_up150_z - RTP_z), potassic K/Th & U/K edges, MT cond_surf clay-cap gradients, and sanitized GDR #1391 thermal/2m-probe/sinter anomalies; (3) Gallardo-Meju (2004) cross-gradient vector alignment |grad(g).grad(m)|/(|grad(g)||grad(m)|) + 1.5 km potential-field & 58-deg updip-migrated phase-tilt strike worms; (4) Two-stage strictly Out-of-Fold HistGradientBoosting synthesis with Stage-2 2D axial probability worms + collar-tempered (d_vis >= 800 m plateau) directional fault-tip & relay-ramp transfer, allocated via exact 300 m triangular-kernel Minoux lazy-greedy submodular coverage (CELF, 37,654 binary {0,1} dots outside EDT > 2.05 px).
ranked_hypotheses.why_missing_from_catalogue: In the NW Great Basin, isolated planar mid-segments of tall range-front master faults are already mapped in existing_faults.tif and are often hydrologically sealed by clay gouge. By contrast, distributed intra-basin synthetic/antithetic (antislope) grabens, horse-tail tip splays, en-echelon relay ramps, and conjugate Walker-Lane / Basin-and-Range fault intersections partition slip across multiple short, sub-meter piedmont scarps and shallow buried basement steps below traditional airphoto mapping thresholds (<2 m scarp height), while hosting >93% of Great Basin blind geothermal vents and permeable upflow conduits (Faulds & Hinz, 2015).
named_non_fault_mimic_processes: Incised dendritic alluvial-fan washes and arroyo banks (suppressed via cross_max denominator, crest-toe dipole symmetry, and 1.1 km flank-subtracted axial worm coherence)
Rugged mountain-interior bedrock crags and glacial/talus cliffs (suppressed via relief normalization step_max/sqrt(relief+9) and piedmont slope/depth interaction)

Circular Cenozoic basaltic/rhyolitic volcanic plugs, caldera ring dikes, and pluton roofs (suppressed via Gallardo-Meju cross-gradient curl |grad(g) x grad(m)| vs linear 1.5 km potential-field worm elongation)
Interstate I-80, railroad embankments, and playa levee berms (suppressed via TIGER/Line 2024 road-corridor proximity indicator)
Playa evaporite brines and transported outwash thermal plumes (suppressed by requiring structural-intersection worm I_vent + shallow TMI_up150 - RTP demagnetization corroboration)
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_existing_repo: ApartGEMSDOE1 v1 (H-APART-1, HOLDOUT-DTI 0.0523, live 0.0525) used single-pixel quantile ranks on only 3 of 12 LiDAR bands, lacked all 2D multi-azimuth strike-worm operators, lacked the orthogonal 2nd-azimuth structural-intersection detector I_vent = sqrt(W_(1)*W_perp), lacked shallow magnetite-oxidation TMI_up150 - RTP and Galleria-Meju cross-gradient coupling, lacked Stage-2 OOF 2D axial probability context, suffered mountain-slope bias (median dot slope 11.93 deg, far-field piedmont recall 0.0059), and blurred ridges prior to allocation.
